title: Settings grouped by user goal
summary: Organize settings around understandable user goals and consequences rather than internal services, database models, or engineering ownership.
problem: Settings pages become dumping grounds where unrelated controls are grouped by implementation rather than what users are trying to accomplish.
use_when: A product exposes multiple preferences, account controls, access controls, or integrations
Users need to revisit settings over time
avoid_when: There are only a few simple settings that fit clearly in one small view
rationale: User-goal grouping improves scanning and makes consequences easier to predict.
Dangerous or rare controls should not compete visually with routine preferences.

use_if: A product exposes multiple preferences, account controls, access controls, or integrations
Users need to revisit settings over time
prefer_alternatives_if: A setting belongs in the immediate context where its effect is understood better

requirements: Use headings and landmarks to make groups navigable.
Keep labels and current values programmatically associated.
Do not make toggles ambiguous about what on and off mean.
Keep dangerous account or billing actions separated from routine preferences.
Show save semantics clearly: instant, explicit, or pending.
